items.statement: disconnect_cache rejects the no-flush plus pass-through combination, opens the control device, maps no_flush to flush_data, and submits KCAS_IOCTL_DISCONNECT_CACHE.
The disconnect ioctl resolves the cache ID to a name and passes the pass-through and inverted flush flag into cache_mngt_disconnect_cache, which validates, acquires, quiesces, and stops the cache.

The kernel path rejects the invalid no-flush plus pass-through combination and standby or incomplete caches, conditionally flushes, and only in pass-through mode captures exported objects, drains outstanding I/O, and purges metadata.
Disconnect first enables the cache no-dirty state and optionally flushes, then switches exported objects to pass-through and freezes their queues before stop processing.

The path acquires the named cache reference, releases it on precondition failures, and on success deposits exported objects, stops the cache, then unfreezes and releases the captured pass-through list.
Both userspace and kernel reject no-flush combined with pass-through; userspace otherwise encodes the default as flush_data=true, while the kernel rejects standby and incomplete cache states.
Cache drain bridges an asynchronous callback to an interruptible completion wait, while cache stop runs through a finish thread and may continue asynchronously if the wait is interrupted.

Userspace distinguishes an interrupted flush from write-cache and generic failures; kernel cleanup clears pass-through state, unfreezes queues, releases captured objects, unlocks, restores dirty-data admission, and drops the cache reference as applicable.

items.description: Disconnect first prevents new dirty data and, unless no-flush is requested, flushes a running cache before taking the management lock.
items.statement: cache_mngt_disconnect_cache sets no-dirty before the management lock and, when flushing is enabled, flushes a running cache and aborts through cleanup if that flush fails.
